title: Data Center & Networking Daily Briefing
description: AI fabrics and enterprise networking, data center capacity, power and cooling, and AI storage.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 22–29. New: Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 28 on standalone Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud and published Stream benchmark results from a local Vera server. The Oct. 21 Google Virgo, A5X, DSX, Lustre, and WWT-DDN items were removed because they are older than seven days. No new NetApp product release was found. No separate power or enterprise-switching announcement dated Oct. 28–29 was found.

items.headline: NVIDIA says Meta will deploy more Vera Rubin racks with Spectrum-X and BlueField-4
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 26 that Meta intends to expand deployment of Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs for what NVIDIA called next-generation AI agents, and that Meta will deploy Spectrum-X Ethernet and BlueField-4 for network efficiency and throughput. The same announcement says the companies will consider additional work on OpenShell and on Sentry, which NVIDIA describes as monitoring for agent behavior. NVIDIA also said it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. The release frames the infrastructure work as support for Muse and the Muse family of models.

items.headline: NVIDIA says Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs are generally available on Oracle Cloud
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 27 that Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs are generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and that the companies plan to expand OCI Superclusters with Vera Rubin NVL72 to multi-gigawatt scale. NVIDIA said those superclusters combine NVL72 racks, Oracle Acceleron networking with Spectrum-X Ethernet using Spectrum-6 switches and BlueField-4 DPUs, and gigawatt-class power and cooling, and that each rack connects 72 GPUs with NVLink. OCI also plans an HGX Rubin NVL8 with eight Rubin GPUs, two 64-core Intel Xeon 6 CPUs, 4 TB of DDR5 memory, and 6.4 Tbps of RDMA networking. NVIDIA said OpenAI has trained and served GPT-6 Astra on an OCI Supercluster with more than 100,000 Blackwell GPUs in Abilene, and that OpenAI is bringing Vera CPUs on OCI into production for agentic sandbox workloads.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion of debt for GPUs due in 2027
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 27 that Elon Musk wrote on X on Oct. 25 that SpaceX had closed $40 billion of debt for GPUs, and that he later said the borrowing is primarily callable debt for purchases arriving in the first and second quarters of 2027 and is not a major factor this quarter. Tom's Hardware says Musk tied the financing to SpaceX having investment-grade status and revenue from Starlink and launch, and that he wrote debt markets have largely shut off companies without substantial revenue outside AI data centers. The article quotes CFO Bret Johnsen, from SpaceX's third-quarter 2026 earnings call, expecting $35 billion to $40 billion of capital expenditure in the fourth quarter. Tom's Hardware says it is still unclear whether "closed" means investors agreed to final pricing, and that Musk did not confirm which GPU models or quantities the debt covers.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: a local Vera server more than doubled Stream bandwidth versus dual Xeon 6
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 28 that Nvidia and Oracle have made Vera Rubin NVL72 and standalone Vera CPUs generally available on OCI Superclusters. In tests on a local Vera server, not on OCI, Tom's Hardware said Stream triad bandwidth was more than double that of a dual Intel Xeon 6980P system using MRDIMMs at 8,800 MT/s, and it cited Nvidia's figure of 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth. Tom's Hardware said Oracle will also offer an HGX NVL8 with eight Rubin GPUs on a dual 64-core Intel Xeon 6 host with 4 TB of DDR5. The outlet said these tests are part of a larger review it has not yet published.

items.headline: NVIDIA launches Minerva, an AIOps platform for finding AI-factory failures earlier
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 22 that Minerva connects telemetry from GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers, and workloads, then uses machine learning to detect anomalies, predict failures, and group related alerts into one incident. NVIDIA says it builds a knowledge graph of GPUs, SuperNICs, switches, cables, and jobs, and includes an assistant that can recommend a fix or call infrastructure APIs. IREN is using it, and Aolani, Bitdeer AI, IBM, Jio, Lambda, Quake AI, and Tesla plan to deploy it. Dell Technologies, Lenovo, and Supermicro will offer Minerva in their AI-factory operations portfolios.
